L’héritage de Jagmeet Singh, premier che: The legacy of Jagmeet Singh, the first racialized leader of a political party
On explore comment la disparition du che: We explore how the Sikh community and racialized people are reacting to the federal leader’s exit from politics.

Les élections fédérales se sont conclues: The federal election is over, marked in particular by the crushing defeat of the New Democratic Party and the announced resignation of its leader, Jagmeet Singh. At La Converse, we wondered how the Sikh community, to which he belongs, and racialized people were taking the exit of a federal party leader from the political scene.
Je me suis donc rendue à Parc-Extension,: So I went to Parc-Extension in Montréal to put the question to residents of this cosmopolitan neighbourhood. I also spoke with a former NDP candidate who was inspired by the politician.
Lorsque Jagmeet Singh a pris la tête du: When Jagmeet Singh became leader of the New Democratic Party (NDP) in 2017, he became the first racialized man to lead a federal political party in Canada. It was a historic moment in a country often seen as a model of diversity, but slow to reflect that reality in its institutions. After he announced his resignation on Monday, at the end of election night, some Montrealers praised his contribution to better representation of diversity.
« C’est dur, mais nous ne sommes vaincus: “It’s hard, but we are only defeated if we stop fighting,” Jagmeet Singh said in his speech on federal election night, Monday. “We are only defeated if we believe those who tell us that we can never dream of a better, fairer, more compassionate Canada.” Wearing a bubblegum-pink turban, the politician struggled to contain his emotion as he announced his resignation as leader of the New Democratic Party. Behind him, his wife let a few tears fall.
La décision semblait inévitable, après l: The decision seemed inevitable after his party’s rout in the federal election, in which it lost 18 seats. The NDP is now reduced to seven MPs, well below the 12 seats needed to keep official party status in the House of Commons. The New Democrats were wiped out in many regions, including their traditional strongholds. Mr. Singh himself lost his seat, and with it, a certain moral authority. The man who had promised to “make Canada fairer” is leaving a party reduced to a fraction of the influence it had under Jack Layton in 2011, when it had 103 MPs.
Le départ de Jagmeet Singh marque la fin: Jagmeet Singh’s departure closes a chapter in Canadian politics: that of a charismatic leader, ideologically firm but strategically isolated, who never managed to turn the sympathy he inspired into a lasting electoral breakthrough. As the first party leader from a minority group, however, he broke a glass ceiling.
<strong>« Jagmeet Singh a permis de chan: “Jagmeet Singh helped change the way people see our community a little”
Deux jours plus tard, dans le quartier d: Two days later, in the Parc-Extension neighbourhood in Montréal, some people regret the politician’s exit. Many first- and second-generation immigrants from Punjab who, like Jagmeet Singh, are Sikh live in this working-class neighbourhood. Under the spring sun finally lighting up the city after weeks of grey skies, parents wait for their children outside Barthélemy-Vimont elementary school.
Parmi eux, plusieurs hommes arborent des: Among them, several men wear brightly coloured turbans. The dastar is worn by some practising Sikhs, followers of the world’s fifth-largest religion, wrapped around hair they never cut, as a symbol of their connection with the divine.
« C’est dommage, mais c’est logique, vu: “It’s a shame, but it makes sense, given the election results. I’m not very political, but it’s true that Jagmeet Singh helped change the way people see our community a little,” says Amar, waving at his daughter, who is looking for him. “Many Canadians didn’t know our beliefs, thought we were Muslims or something else. But when he was elected, he talked about us, he explained why he wears the dastar and a beard; that’s a good thing. It doesn’t stop some people from being racist, but it’s still better than nothing.” Holding his child’s hand, he then heads home.
À quelques mètres de l’école, de l’autre: A few metres from the school, across the street, is the Sikh community centre Gurdwara Guru Nanak Darbar. On a bench, a man with a white beard is enjoying the beautiful late afternoon. “Of course I know who he is! He did a lot of good for our community,” is all he says, visibly uncomfortable. The older man points to the park next door, just behind the school: “Over there you’ll find people to talk to.”
Il est 16 h. À cette heure-là, les cris: It’s 4 p.m. At this hour, the shouts and laughter of children echo through Parc Saint-Roch, separated from Parc Jarry by the railway. While toddlers run and jump from one play structure to another, three women chat on a shaded bench. “I really think it’s important to have people who look like us in politics. Even if we’re not interested in everything that goes on federally, I think someone like him understands better what we live through,” says Bhani.
La jeune mère regrette son départ, mais: The young mother regrets his departure but hopes others will follow. “A woman like us would be even better!” she slips in, setting off laughter from her two less talkative friends. Even though she doesn’t think it can change everything overnight, Bhani is convinced these advances matter symbolically.
À la sortie du métro Parc, Noor revient: Outside the Parc metro station, Noor is coming back from her job at a grocery store. After her law classes, the young woman of Pakistani origin works to pay for her studies. “When you come from a diverse background, it’s not always easy to be ambitious. There aren’t many role models, but Jagmeet Singh was one,” says Noor, who nevertheless voted Liberal to block the Conservatives.
Au-delà de la politique, elle espère que: Beyond politics, she hopes racialized Canadians will reach more positions of power in the years to come. “It’s not just a question of politics. In businesses, in courts, in the media, it’s rare to see people who look like us in the top positions. It’s really important that this changes, because we’re citizens like everyone else; and in 2025, the question shouldn’t even come up,” she says.
Lorsqu’elle était jeune, Noor a subi du: When she was young, Noor experienced racism from her schoolmates. “Some parents must say things in front of their kids, and the kids repeat them. It’s often ignorance, but it hurt me a lot, because I didn’t see any difference between different skin colours,” she recalls. Today, she says she is no longer “ashamed” of her origins and dreams of a great career as a lawyer that will open the way for young girls in her community, who are underrepresented in the profession. A bit like Jagmeet Singh.
Mais d’autres Montréalais sont moins dit: But other Montrealers are less effusive about the politician. Several people we spoke to didn’t know him or barely knew him, and had “no opinion” on the matter.
À quelques rues de là, Adil discute avec: A few streets away, Adil is chatting with a friend at a café table. The name Jagmeet Singh doesn’t mean much to him, but the photo does. “He was one of the candidates in the election!” he says proudly. “But I’m not allowed to vote yet, so I don’t really know the names,” explains the man in his thirties, who arrived from Algeria a year ago.
Mécanicien et père de deux enfants, il d: A mechanic and father of two, he says he appreciates that Canada has politicians like Jagmeet Singh. “I have family in France, and over there it’s a lot more complicated to go into politics if you’re Arab or Black, for example. I feel like here it’s more open; and that’s a good thing,” says Adil. Happy with his immigration despite the “difficulties,” he wants his children to be able to become whatever they want, without putting up barriers for themselves.
Au-delà des considérations politiques, l: Political considerations aside, the simple fact that Jagmeet Singh was able to become a federal party leader is a step forward for younger generations from diverse backgrounds, Adil believes.
<strong>« Voir un député devenir chef de: “Seeing an MP become party leader as a minority was very inspiring to me”
« Savoir qu’on n’a plus de chef de parti: “Knowing that we no longer have a federal party leader from a diverse background in Canada is upsetting. He was someone with a real commitment who truly wanted life to be affordable for everyone.” An activist since 2020 and the NDP candidate in 2021 in the riding of Dorval—Lachine—LaSalle, where she grew up, Fabiola Ngamaleu Teumeni says she saw in Jagmeet Singh an important symbol in a political landscape that is still very homogeneous.
« Les personnes issues des minorités son: “People from minorities are very underrepresented in the House of Commons, so seeing an MP become party leader as a minority was very inspiring to me. This year, eight Black people were elected; so it’s an issue that remains real,” says Teumeni, who moved from Germany at age three and is of Cameroonian origin.
Malgré son attachement à ce que Jagmeet: Despite her attachment to what Jagmeet Singh represents, the 24-year-old psychology student nevertheless believes his departure was inevitable. “I think it’s a logical decision. He ran two major campaigns, but he didn’t manage to move the needle in Quebec.” The party did indeed win only one seat in the province, Alexandre Boulerice’s.
Selon elle, le chef du NPD a raté sa cam: In her view, the NDP leader missed the mark in his campaign on some crucial issues. “With everything that’s been happening since Trump’s election, Jagmeet Singh didn’t talk enough about these threats and the fear Canadians feel. He didn’t necessarily present himself as a third option for standing up to the United States, even though that’s what was talked about most during this campaign.” The young woman nonetheless stayed true to her values by voting NDP.
Fabiola Ngamaleu Teumeni espère maintena: Fabiola Ngamaleu Teumeni now hopes to see a new generation of leaders emerge, more rooted in the realities of communities and better reflecting the diversity of Canadians. “I’d like to see him back in the House of Commons because he’s a good support, but as leader, I think it’s time for someone new – a woman maybe,” she says with a laugh.
Si l’arrivée de Jagmeet Singh au sein de: If Jagmeet Singh’s arrival among the power elite didn’t come without difficulty, the arrival of a woman, let alone a racialized woman, would be a new milestone.
<strong>Une carrière politique marquée p: A political career marked by racist attacks
Né à Scarborough, en Ontario, dans une f: Born in Scarborough, Ontario, to a family from Punjab, Jagmeet Singh grew up in a society where the place of women and minorities was even less visible than it is today. He studied at Western University and Osgoode Hall before becoming a criminal lawyer. Elected as a provincial MPP in 2011, Jagmeet Singh quickly rose through the ranks of the Ontario NDP, until he won the federal leadership race in 2017 on the first ballot.
« Des enfants me frappaient parce que je: “Kids beat me up because I didn’t look like them. That racism marked my childhood,” the new party leader confided on television. Riding his bike to Parliament and speaking openly about racism, Jagmeet Singh was quickly noticed and brought a breath of fresh air. By becoming party leader, he allowed the representation of diversity to finally enter the upper echelons of politics. But this symbol was not to everyone’s taste in Canada.
Quelques semaines avant son accession à: A few weeks before he became leader, in September 2017, <l1>a video</l1> circulated on social media. In it, a woman accuses Jagmeet Singh of wanting to “impose Sharia” on Canada at a public NDP rally. She apparently confuses the Muslim religion, with which <l2>Sharia</l2> is associated, with the Sikh religion.
Une erreur qui montre l’ignorance de nom: A mistake that shows the ignorance of many citizens, even though Canada has the world’s second-largest Sikh community after India. According to the 2021 census, 771,790 people in the country report being Sikh.
Égal à lui-même, le chef de parti réagit: True to himself, the party leader responded to the attack with a message of calm: “We don’t want to be intimidated by hate. We don’t want hate to ruin a positive event.” He then spoke directly to the heckler. “We welcome you. We love you. We support you. We believe in your rights,” he assured her to an ovation from the crowd. But the discrimination did not stop on the night of his election.
Lors de sa première entrevue nationale e: In his first national interview as the new NDP leader, he was pressed repeatedly about the <l1>bombing of an Air India plane</l1> in 1985 because of his background. The explosion of a bomb on board, which killed all 329 people aboard, is attributed to Sikh separatists. This obviously has nothing to do with Jagmeet Singh, especially since he was only a child at the time of the tragedy.
Plusieurs voix au sein du parti et dans: Several voices within the party and the Sikh community then denounced biased treatment and argued that a white politician would never have been asked to answer for crimes committed by coreligionists or fellow citizens of the same origin.
À plusieurs reprises, Jagmeet Singh a ai: Jagmeet Singh has thus faced racist attacks on several occasions. Another incident took place in 2019 when a man asked him to “cut off his turban” at a rally. “Canadians look like all kinds of people, and that’s what’s beautiful,” the politician replied, as calm as ever.
Durant cette dernière campagne fédérale,: During this last federal campaign, Mr. Singh revealed that he had considered leaving political life in December 2023, after receiving death threats deemed credible while his wife was pregnant with their second child. “It was really a scary time. I had a knot in my stomach. For the first few days, I stayed in the basement because I’d been advised not to go near the windows,” the politician said at a press conference in London, two days before the vote, <l1>CBC reports</l1>.
Des menaces prises d’autant plus au séri: The threats were taken all the more seriously because the Canadian Sikh separatist leader Hardeep Singh Nijjar was assassinated in Surrey in June 2023. The Canadian government attributes the killing to Indian agents, which India denies.
Dans ce contexte, la décision de Jagmeet: In this context, Jagmeet Singh’s decision to stay, despite being placed under police protection, reflects the personal sacrifices that taking part in political life still demands, particularly of figures from minority communities.
Sous la direction de M. Singh, le NPD a: Under Mr. Singh’s leadership, the NDP bet on a progressive platform focused on social justice, workers’ rights and expanded social supports. Unable to break through in voting intentions, the NDP leader nevertheless managed to take advantage of a minority Liberal government. In 2022, he struck a confidence-and-supply agreement with the Liberals, guaranteeing them New Democrat support in exchange for concrete measures.
La défaite de 2025 a été brutale. Pourta: The 2025 defeat was brutal. Yet Mr. Singh’s supporters point out that his time at the helm of the NDP anchored certain social priorities in the federal political agenda. Among the successes attributed to Jagmeet Singh are the national dental care program and progress on pharmacare. But this strategy, hailed on the left as pragmatic, nevertheless damaged his image with many voters, according to some observers. The New Democrat, they say, had stopped embodying a real opposition.
Son refus de voter une motion de censure: His refusal to vote for a non-confidence motion against the Trudeau government, while the Bloc Québécois was willing, was seen as a desire to preserve his influence rather than force the government’s fall. A decision that, in December 2024, sealed his political fate, according to some commentators.
Aujourd’hui, alors que le NPD entame un: Today, as the NDP begins a new cycle of rebuilding, Jagmeet Singh’s legacy remains hard to assess. He did not lead his party to power, but he changed the face of Canadian politics forever.
En Inde, plusieurs journaux comme <em><l: In India, several newspapers such as The Indian Express welcomed the removal of a “major obstacle to resetting diplomatic relations between India and Canada,” while the television network NDTV sees the politician’s resignation as “good news for India.” The country, which opposes Sikh independence aims, had indeed looked unfavourably on Justin Trudeau’s closeness to the NDP leader.
